_readme: Add an app by copying the item marked "template": true, pasting it into this "items" array, filling it in, and removing the "template": true line. (If the file is repo-hosted, commit it under /downloads/ or another folder build.sh copies into dist/.)
A download 'url' can be a repo-relative path (e.g. /downloads/MyApp-1.2.0.exe) OR a full external URL (e.g. https://github.com/you/app/releases/download/...).

An item with "template": true renders as a non-clickable TEMPLATE reference card at the bottom of the page and is excluded from search/sort/filter and the count. Keys starting with '_' are ignored entirely.
Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD). 'updated' drives the Newest/Oldest sort; the newest changelog entry should match the current 'version'. Set "featured": true to pin an app to the top with a badge.

items.name: Lyric Chunker
items.tagline: Blender add-on + Fusion comp generator for the music visualizer pipeline
items.description: Type delimited lyrics, get styled 3D text split into per-syllable chunk objects, batch-render each chunk as a transparent 16-bit PNG with a JSON timing manifest per line, then generate a pasteable Fusion node graph (color-flip + bounce, timed from the manifest) for DaVinci Resolve. The bundle zip has both tools; the add-on installs via Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > Install from Disk, the comp generator runs with plain Python 3.

notes: Add travel motion: elements that hop word to word and land on the beat (LyricChunker@150d85b)
Add reactor elements: images that bounce on chunk timing (LyricChunker@b599f03)
Add Tap Timing, viewport timing preview, and a Resolve build script (LyricChunker@ea91f25)
Let the untimed cascade be set in frames as well as seconds (LyricChunker@7b5bd32)
Expose the untimed cascade length in the Timing panel (LyricChunker@df89acf)
Pin each comp Loader to its own frame of the detected sequence (LyricChunker@2e89c45)
Cascade untimed lines across a default span in generated comps (LyricChunker@e867b39)
Premultiply Loader alpha to kill edge fringing in comps (LyricChunker@c9516a9)
Serialize comp Loaders the way Fusion saves them (LyricChunker@4890677)
Hold comp Loader stills far past the line span (LyricChunker@45e45e7)
Generate Fusion comps from a panel button, no terminal needed (LyricChunker@ffa7497)
Show the full selected lyric line wrapped under the panel list (LyricChunker@52396dc)
Type lyric lines straight into the panel with a browsable line list (LyricChunker@16f9463)
Ship the comp generator alongside the add-on as a downloads bundle (LyricChunker@5470c22)
Bake the project house style into the default template (LyricChunker@b763031)
First release on the downloads hub.
Syllable-chunk generation from delimited lyric lines with template-based styling.
Batch renders each chunk as a transparent 16-bit PNG, per-line output folders.

items.name: OSRS Soundboard
items.tagline: Desktop soundboard, music player and sample grabber for Old School RuneScape audio
items.description: A standalone desktop app — not a browser tab — with two tabs of its own: a pad grid of every OSRS sound effect that fires instantly and overlaps when you hammer it, and a searchable library of the music tracks and jingles with a full transport bar. Both share one mixer, so a track can run under the board while you fire effects over it. Save 4×4 or 8×8 boards and play them from the number and QWERTY rows, drag sounds straight out into REAPER, Resolve or Discord, and let it match each sound to its wiki artwork. The app ships empty and assembles its own library from the OSRS Wiki on first run: sound effects and short jingles are stored locally so pads have no latency, and music streams on demand rather than filling 7 GB of disk. Esc stops every voice instantly.

notes: Level-up jingles now show their skill icon, for all 23 skills.
Match artwork for engine-style names like "100 goblin falls" by digging the entity out of the filename.
Sort the board by artwork first, A–Z or length — alphabetical used to bury everything behind hundreds of numbered quest sounds.
Cleaner fallback tiles: a leading number no longer eats both initials.
Search sounds by what they are, not just their filename — searching "being hit" or "special attack" now finds the right pad.
Pads show what the sound is underneath the name.
Filter by whether a sound has wiki artwork, with a live count of how many do not.
Re-match artwork on its own from the Update button, without re-downloading any audio.
Match artwork for "Equip <item>" sounds, which were previously all discarded.
One Windows installer instead of two — the MSI only mattered for managed deployment, so it is gone.
Saved boards: 4×4 and 8×8 layouts, Alt+1–9 to switch, slots 1–16 bound to the number and QWERTY rows.
Drag sounds out into other apps, with grab handles on pads and library rows and an optional whole-pad gesture. Files are handed over under their real names.
Wiki sprite matching: sounds are linked to their artwork via the SFX Project index, with an inline search to override any icon by hand.
Sound effects now carry their in-game sound ID and config name, and both are searchable.
First release. Tauri desktop shell; the installer adds a desktop shortcut.
First-run setup reads the wiki file index and downloads sound effects and short jingles, resumable if you quit halfway.
Soundboard tab: virtualized pad grid, overlapping polyphonic playback, per-pad volume and pitch.
Library tab: virtualized list with crossfading transport, variant chips, favourites.
Search with cat: filters, current-only and length filters, Esc panic.
